title: DEGREES OF DECEPTION: How AI will disrupt higher education forever with Edward Ning
description: Send us Fan Mail Discover how artificial intelligence is poised to disrupt higher education with ex-Baidu senior manager, tech-optimist and rooftop garder Edward Ning (check out the video links at the bottom of the show notes). Gain insights into the future of academia as we discuss cutting-edge applications like automated transcription services and advanced search engines that boost productivity and accessibility. Eddy's vast experience, spanning before the ChatGPT era of AI sheds light on the transformative potential of AI tools and their role in reshaping educational practices for the better. We explore fascinating real-world projects, including higher education using AI in collaboration with a university's railway transportation department to develop a subway camera image capture and analysis system. This project highlights how AI can enhance security and efficiency beyond human capabilities, but also hints at the sinister side of the AI led surveillance state. Together, we address the broader implications of AI integration, such as job displacement fears and evolving job roles, drawing parallels to recent technological advancements like cloud computing. From the student perspective, we emphasize the importance of critical thinking and problem-solving skills in the AI era. Hear why it's crucial for schools to teach not just the use of AI, but also the understanding of its principles. We reflect on the future of universities, the enduring value of face-to-face interactions, and ethical considerations. Join us for a thought-provoking discussion on how AI is set to shape the future of higher education and empower the next generation of learners. Eddy's rooftop garden series (CGTN): 'Oh! My Greens' Ep. 1: How to build a vibrant garden in Beijing? 'Oh! My Greens' Ep. 2: She creates an ecosystem with potted plants 'Oh! My Greens' Ep. 3: Grab the autumn in Beijing's hutong garden
summary: Eddie Ning, a former AI industry professional turned jobseeker, joins for the first education episode on higher education. The conversation covers stealthy background AI like university subway-camera surveillance projects, whether universities survive the AI era, cheating versus tool use, and why both hosts think every student should be encouraged to use every AI tool available.
keyTalkingPoints: Eddie's subway-camera project with a railway university trained models to spot temperature anomalies 24/7 — background AI most people never notice
Eddie's line: AI is a tool, humans rule — but students must embrace it, because graduates who fear AI will be worse off
The hosts test AI in their own workflows: Claude brainstorms episodes, Perplexity researches with linked papers, custom GPTs write Suno lyrics
Matt's housemate once pasted 500 extra words into his dissertation — essay mills existed before ChatGPT and their human writers have already been replaced
On universities: Matt asks whether teaching and research should be split apart; Jimmy sees research institutions surviving but vocational education expanding

jimmy: Background, stealthy AI is his real fear — the gradual erosion of jobs nobody notices until the security guard is gone
AI in education is a supplementary tool, not a teacher replacement; motivated learners win and lazy learners lose either way
Universities are research institutions as much as schools — but we could use far more vocational education
AI can enhance critical thinking when users interrogate its output instead of swallowing it
matt: Every student should be encouraged to use every AI tool they can get their hands on
AI can reduce teacher workload — marking and lesson planning are the front and back end nobody enjoys
The writing-as-thinking argument partly convinces him: the writing process is how many people think
The whole concept of higher education will change completely — hopefully toward richer, practical, face-to-face models
